reelection.rule: Rule: end of the current class term in legislators-current.yaml. Class 2 ends 2027-01-03. The November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file does not store the election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 20. Nay or No: 20. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 40 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 44 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

finance.disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
finance.cycle_rule: Senate filings use the two-year cycle of the next election. the current term ends 2027-01-03, so the preceding November election is 2026.
finance.scope_note: Figures are committee receipts and itemized Schedule A for this two-year cycle only. This is not career fundraising. Schedule E outside spending is not included.
finance.contributor_note: Itemized Schedule A receipts for this principal campaign committee and cycle, grouped by contributor name. Memo lines are omitted so an earmark is not counted twice. Unitemized donations are not in this list. Not every Schedule A row was retrieved, so this ranking uses the largest receipts returned and can miss contributors whose gifts are smaller but add up.

running.label: Candidates who filed with the FEC for this seat. Filing is not the same as being on the ballot. Primary results and ballot access are not shown.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: Senate votes 1–262 of the 119th Congress, session 2 (262 votes, January 5, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the Senate LIS.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

party_line.scope: Senate votes 1–262 of the 119th Congress, session 2 (262 votes, January 5, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the Senate LIS.

topics.rule: nomination (PN) in the Senate vote XML

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text:
Best of luck to all the deer hunters heading out to camp this week! Stay safe and enjoy your time in the woods. 🦌
 
https://t.co/z4rQXO1nYn

The 988 hotline has become a vital lifeline for Americans who are struggling with their mental health, especially our veterans living with the invisible wounds of war.

I was proud to help pass a resolution raising awareness of this National Suicide Prevention Hotline in the https://t.co/q4yOOlRdXY

Thanks to the PACT Act, veterans can now receive VA health care benefits for exposure to Agent Orange and toxic burn pits.

I was proud to help pass this long overdue legislation into law, and I thank Michiganders like Michael for working with military families to secure the benefits they earned.

For more than 250 years, Americans have answered the call to serve, putting their lives on the line to defend our nation, preserve our democracy, and protect the freedoms we all hold dear. So, to all of our nation’s veterans: thank you for your service and sacrifice for our https://t.co/HpFvI7fouw

The story of Michigan Army veteran Gerald Elliot is a reminder of our sacred responsibility to care for our veterans and their families.

Thanks to his story, veterans can no longer be denied VA burial benefits if they choose to receive hospice care outside of a VA facility. I was proud to work with Dickinson County Veterans Service Officer Denise Formolo to pass Gerald's Law, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure veterans can access the benefits they earned.

I recently had the chance to see the National Military Monument currently on display in Washington, D.C. It was remarkable to see so many people honoring a loved one who served this nation. I encourage everyone to take a moment this week to thank those who answered the call of duty.

I believe you can't be a great country unless you actually make things, and they’re making great things at Hemlock Semiconductor. The products they make are critical to both U.S. national security and the future of our auto industry here in Michigan. https://t.co/H5qlCZybkR

On National Cat Day, I want to shout out Gerri, who I recently got a chance to meet in Walker. Thank you to the Humane Society of West Michigan, and animal rescues across our state, for all that you do to create a safe harbor for our four-legged friends like Gerri! https://t.co/Cv8GwFoDkN

I've been proud to support the FishPass Project in downtown Traverse City to help preserve vital Great Lakes ecosystems and waterways across the region for years to come. This project is a tremendous example of what we can accomplish when local, state, federal, and tribal https://t.co/L9PHXKLKT1

After 411 days, Henry Ford Genesys nurses reached a contract agreement. They stood together for safer staffing, better working conditions, and the patients they serve.

Growing up in a union household, I know the power of collective bargaining. I stand with Michigan workers.

Michigan never fails to innovate, and the FRIB at MSU is no exception. Since they broke ground on this facility over a decade ago, I have been proud to support their exploration in science and technology. We’ll benefit from the investments made at this facility for decades to come.
Thank you Mayor Behnke for the honor of receiving the key to the city! It's been a privilege to represent and advocate for the Battle Creek community in the U.S. Senate. https://t.co/Z4gcWC2haZ

The American people have watched President Trump enrich himself and his cronies. Members of both parties should be calling out this Administration's corruption - like @SenatorSlotkin is doing. She is simply saying that no one is above the law, and no one should be. https://t.co/AuJAHKBv48

The Federal Protective Service MegaCenter in Battle Creek is critical to our state and our nation. I know that these public servants are an invaluable part of the downtown community and keeping them here in Battle Creek will make sure that expertise stays right here—with minimal https://t.co/IZH8B7qa5a

The Federal Protective Service MegaCenter in Battle Creek is critical to our state and our nation. I know that these public servants are an invaluable part of the downtown community and keeping them here in Battle Creek will make sure that expertise stays right here—with minimal https://t.co/xUkIiDj1sX

Selfridge Air National Guard Base must remain a critical asset to our military and homeland security efforts. I will never stop fighting to make sure the men and women on that base have the tools they need to be successful. https://t.co/jbuCzWJdJw

I am deeply concerned by the escalating situation in Albania. Local authorities must refrain from aggression against peaceful protesters, and everyone on the ground must work to deescalate and prevent further violence. 

Michigan is home to a strong and vibrant Albanian American

Many truck drivers and farmers are now paying nearly double for diesel compared to before Trump’s war with Iran. This Administration must work towards ending this war and bringing costs down. https://t.co/oxszk0F6fR

Thank you to the firefighters and Michigan DNR officials who are continuing to battle the wildfires in the Upper Peninsula right now and keeping folks safe. I encourage everyone to monitor any DNR updates and developments in your area. https://t.co/6jALgVFq4m

The U.S. Navy turned 251 today! As a proud retired Lt. Commander in the U.S. Navy Reserve, I want to recognize all our Navy veterans as well as those sailors currently serving in the fleet at home and abroad. https://t.co/PhDGRWff8m

For more than a century, Berston Field House has been a gathering place for Flint residents. I commend all the folks in the community who are leading the charge to revitalize and expand the field house for future generations, and I was proud to be a federal partner in their efforts.

The Great Lakes Restoration Initiative is the most significant investment ever made to restore and protect our Great Lakes. I’ll keep working in a bipartisan way to get this commonsense bill passed into law to help protect the Great Lakes for future generations. https://t.co/8unmxMdZa2

My heart is with Jewish communities in Michigan and around the world as we mourn the lives lost in the horrific October 7th terrorist attacks three years ago. The attacks and the ongoing war have brought immense pain and suffering, deeply affecting countless Michiganders and their loved ones. As we remember those who were killed and reflect on the profound toll of the conflict, we must stand together against hatred in all its forms, while continuing to work toward a future where all people can live in safety and practice their faith freely without fear.

Exciting progress in downtown Traverse City! Once completed, this pedestrian bridge will give folks a glimpse into the FishPass project that will help protect the Great Lakes ecosystem by sorting local fish from invasive species like sea lamprey. I’m proud to have secured over $22 million to support this project and Traverse City’s economy.
 https://t.co/avGMD05hvE

It’s past time that the Department of Defense treats PFAS contamination with the urgency it deserves. My bipartisan bill would force them to get shovels in the ground and begin cleanup of contaminated sites in Michigan without further delay. https://t.co/33avUSy4Vg

This taxpayer-funded ad campaign is completely unacceptable. President Trump and Republicans in Congress told the American people they needed this money to keep them safe. Instead, the President is using these funds to boost his agenda ahead of the midterm elections. It’s not the first time we’ve seen DHS misuse funds for self-serving commercials, and it has to stop. Americans deserve a Department of Homeland Security that is working to protect our nation – not promote the President and his political allies.

I led nearly three dozen of my colleagues last week calling on Secretary Mullin to drop these requirements, and to halt DHS’s election interference efforts. The court did the right thing, but this clearly shouldn’t have become policy in the first place. Now, FEMA needs to immediately release this funding to help keep communities safe.

Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” sold out many rural hospitals in Michigan by making drastic cuts to Medicaid funding. These health care cuts will make it harder for Michiganders to receive care, and it was all to pay for tax cuts to billionaires.
https://t.co/OOb1lWDQFG

My heart is with the greater Grand Blanc Township community today as we remember the lives lost in last year's mass shooting and fire. I am deeply grateful to the first responders for their bravery that day, and I am inspired by this community's resilience as they break ground on a new chapel.
 
https://t.co/889U6gkFYk

The newly renovated Pontiac Oaks Park is a prime example of what’s possible when federal, state, and local officials work together to achieve a common goal. I want to thank the Oakland County Parks and Recreation Commission for dedicating a new pavilion at the park in my honor. I was proud to celebrate with so many partners who made this beautiful community space a reality.

Very proud that my wife Colleen was honored with the Congressional Families Leadership Award today for her work with @preventcancer’s #CongressionalFamilies Program to increase cancer awareness and early detection. She is truly the most important person in my life, and I am so lucky to be by her side.

Since the beginning of Trump’s war with Iran, Michiganders have watched their gas prices go up and up. Instead of working towards ending this war and bringing costs down, the President is now considering a further escalation of the conflict. I hope the President re-engages and shows clear strategy for the American people.

I’m proud to join Michiganders in recognizing our first PFAS Awareness Week.

PFAS contamination continues to threaten the health of Michiganders, the Great Lakes, and our environment. I'll never stop fighting to clean up contaminated sites, keep PFAS out of our drinking water, and hold polluters accountable.

This week Michiganders are seeing the highest gas prices of the year because of Trump’s war with Iran. 

This Administration must recognize the economic burden this war is putting on hardworking families and get serious about a winning strategy for peace. https://t.co/Vl8Rk4RdiU
Great to talk with @Local4News’s Jason Colthrup at the Detroit Economic Club today! https://t.co/OeG6Hsx05w
Michiganders are paying higher prices because of President Trump’s policies, from the grocery store to the gas station to the doctor’s office. It’s unacceptable. https://t.co/Ms7UrTlxRx
Wishing a peaceful Yom Kippur to all those observing in Michigan and around the world.

Months after Trump declared “total and complete victory” in Iran, this war has now cost American taxpayers at least $40 billion dollars. 

The American people did not ask for this. They asked us to bring costs down. And yet today, we’re in another war in the Middle East that is risking American lives and raising the cost of living. https://t.co/k82ukRsSmM

It was great meeting with so many leaders during CBC week, including Flint @mayorneeley and @CityofDetroit Mayor Sheffield! Thank you to all the Michiganders who brought their voice to the U.S. Capitol and discussed critical issues impacting our communities. https://t.co/IES6bPCL29

Honored to host the Annual Michigan Congressional Black Caucus Breakfast with my friend @SenatorSlotkin this year. I'm blessed to have worked with so many incredible leaders in the CBC over the years, and I will never stop fighting alongside them to build a more just and equitable future in our country.

Artificial intelligence is advancing at an extraordinary pace, and we must slow down its development until we establish commonsense guardrails that ensure this transformational technology is developed safely and responsibly.
 
I’ve worked across the aisle to pass bipartisan legislation establishing safeguards for the federal government’s use of AI, but it’s clear this technology’s impact will be wide-ranging and significant across our entire society. It’s well past time for Congress, the industry, and the Trump Administration to take immediate action and put meaningful standards in place to guide responsible AI innovation.

On POW/MIA Day, we honor the brave servicemembers who gave their lives in defense of our nation, have been held prisoner of war, and those who have not returned home. 
 
Their sacrifice is a debt we can never repay, but must honor by preserving the freedoms and values we hold dear as Americans.

As a society, we have an obligation to provide lifesaving crisis support to every American in every community – and that’s exactly what the 9-8-8 suicide and crisis lifeline does.
 
During National Suicide Prevention Month, I took to the Senate floor to raise awareness of this essential and invaluable resource because no one should ever suffer alone.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
